npcs.name: Kerra Aldar
npcs.idle: Thirty sheep last spring. Nine now.

npcs.name: Tregarth the Hunter
npcs.idle: The moor is wrong this year. Even the wolves know it.

npcs.name: Old Hywel
npcs.idle: My grandfather's grandfather marched with the legion. Some of it, I think, is still marching.

npcs.name: Lieutenant Penhale
npcs.idle: Report to the commander if it's official. Report to me if it's strange.

quests.title: The White She-Wolf
quests.offer:
Wolves took my flock - a few at a time, all spring, then twenty in one night. A white she-wolf leads them. I've seen her on the ridge, watching the fold.

I want her dead. I want her hide on my floor. Will you [hunt her]? Tregarth the hunter knows the moor - he'll tell you where she dens, even if he won't like it.
quests.summary: Kerra Aldar wants the white she-wolf that led the pack against her flock hunted down.

steps.text: The fold's torn open. But the tracks are wrong for hunting wolves - they come in running, from the west, as if something were driving them.

steps.goal: Ask Tregarth the hunter about the white wolf
steps.say: The white bitch? I know her. She's been on this moor eight years and never touched a sheep till this spring. Something's pushing the packs east - the [death stalkers] are out of the woods and hungry. Kill a few of those and see where the wolves go.

steps.goal: Hunt the death stalkers on the western moor
steps.text: Gorged, every one of them - and in the last one's den, a pile of small white bones. Wolf cubs. The she-wolf's den is close.
She's there. Thin as a rake, white fur gone grey with mud, standing over two cubs - all that's left of her litter. She doesn't run. She just watches you.

steps.say:
There she is. Followed you up.

She took Kerra's sheep, right enough. And she took them because the stalkers took her cubs and there was nothing else on the moor. Now the stalkers are dealt with. She'll go back west, or I'm no hunter.

Kerra asked for her hide. I won't do it for you. [Kill her], or [let her go].

options.say: ...Your call. Make it clean, at least.
Good. Go tell Kerra. She'll shout. Let her shout. She'll understand by spring.

steps.text: She doesn't fight much. The cubs run off into the heather.

steps.say:
You LET HER GO? I asked for -

...Death stalkers. Her own cubs. Gods. Tregarth told me the same and I wouldn't hear it.

Fine. FINE. If a single sheep goes missing, I'm coming to find you. Here - for the stalkers, if not the wolf.

She's dead? Good. Good.

Then why do I feel like this. Tregarth told me why she came. I wish he hadn't. Here. Take your reward and the hide - I don't want it on my floor after all.

mercy.text: For the stalkers, if not the wolf.

revenge.text: Take it. Take all of it.

quests.title: The Drowned Ninth
quests.offer:
Every autumn the drowned legion marches the old road south - ghosts, skeletons, whatever they are. Every autumn somebody from my family lays a wreath on their road. My grandfather's grandfather was one of them, so they say.

This year my grandson Kit laid it. He didn't come back. The [lieutenant] says it's not army business. Will you [find Kit]?

topics.lieutenant: Penhale. Young. Reads too much. He might listen.

quests.summary: Old Hywel's grandson Kit laid a wreath on the road where the drowned legion marches, and did not come home.

steps.goal: Ask Lieutenant Penhale about the legion
steps.say: Not official business, no. But I've read the old reports. The Ninth went into the marshes after a raiding king and never came out. They march the old road south every year, back to the barrow where their [centurion] lies. Anyone on the road goes with them.

steps.goal: Walk the legion's old road south
steps.text: The road is churned by hundreds of feet that left no prints. Skeletons in rusted mail stand guard along it, still at attention.
Kit's wreath, trodden flat. The tracks of the legion lead west across the moor - to the barrow of the giant dead.

steps.goal: Follow the legion west to the great barrow
steps.text: A giant skeleton stands at the barrow mouth holding a legion's eagle - and beside it, in a red cloak, a pale young man holding the standard pole. Kit.
The centurion's bones fall into a heap. The legionaries stop where they stand and kneel, waiting for an order.

stages.name: Centurion of the Drowned Ninth
stages.announce: The giant turns. 'Standard-bearer! Hold the line!' Kit doesn't move. The legion does.
stages.success: Centurion of the Drowned Ninth falls.

steps.say:
I couldn't put it down. The standard. I tried. They needed someone to carry it and I was there and I just... couldn't put it down.

It's lighter now. They're waiting. They're waiting for someone to tell them [what to do].

steps.goal: Decide what becomes of the legion's standard
steps.say:
The standard - the eagle. If we [lay it to rest] in the barrow with the centurion, I think they'll sleep. All of them. No more marching.

Or we [bring it home]. Grandfather would - gods, he'd weep. The Eagle of the Ninth, in our house. It's ours too, isn't it? Our family's?

options.say: You're right. You're right. Here - help me. ... There. Listen. Do you hear that? Nothing. Nothing at all.
Grandfather will never believe it. Come on. Let's go before they change their minds.

steps.goal: Bring Kit home to Old Hywel
steps.say:
He's home. And the legion's asleep - he says you laid the eagle down with them.

Four hundred years, that road. My family will still lay a wreath, mind. Out of respect. But we won't be going to find anyone.

steps.goal: Bring Kit home to Old Hywel
steps.say:
The Eagle of the Ninth. In my house.

...I heard marching last night, you know. Faint. Coming up the road from the marsh, where it's never come before. Kit hears it too. Take something, quick, before I change my mind about all of this.
